conviction_note: Findings sum to +1.2 (a late-season heat tailwind, a 10% holder buying steadily at ~$5.10, and possible capital or strategic news, against two straight EPS misses and soft channel signals from Watsco and Chemours). The scaled number is slightly negative: p_up 47 because this stock has fallen on five prints in a row, which has veto power over the small positive evidence, times abs 12 (the 11.7% median reaction; ATM IV of 75.8% against 25.7% realised vol implies a large event premium). The gap between the two numbers is that reaction history, not an inconsistency.
bar: Q3 2026 EPS consensus $0.11, from two agreeing sources: Benzinga (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/HDSN/earnings-forecasts) and Earnings Whispers (https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/HDSN). The revenue bar is disputed: $78.3M Benzinga, $75.51M Earnings Whispers, $77.96M Yahoo (https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/HDSN/analysis/). Company guide (Q2 release, 2026-08-05): FY2026 gross margin cut to 'low-to-mid twenties' from mid-twenties; H1 was 23% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000925528/000110465926091092/tm2622080d1_ex99-1.htm). Comparison quarter Q3 2025: revenue $74.0M, GM 32.0%, EPS $0.27 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/925528/000110465925107007/tm2530368d1_ex99-1.htm). Revenue-based findings are capped small because the revenue bar is disputed.
positioning_check: Short interest 2,594,444 shares, 6.28% of float, 8.6 days to cover, record date 2026-10-15, down 3.5% from 2,688,167 (MarketBeat, FINRA publication 2026-10-26: https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/HDSN/short-interest). It was about 1.67M shares (2.5 DTC) at 2026-05-29 (https://equibles.com/stocks/hdsn/short-interest), so shorts built through the summer. 8.6 days to cover on 334k shares a day is a moderately crowded short, so negatives are shrunk. Skew: unavailable, the chain is unusable (ATM spread 108% of mid). ATM IV is 75.8% for the 2026-11-20 expiry against 25.7% 20-day realised. Put/call OI is 0.36. Hartree Partners (10%+ holder) has bought in the open market every few weeks at about $5.10.

findings.finding: Late-season heat was stronger than last year. AGA cooling degree days for the four weeks ending 8 Aug to 29 Aug 2026 total 324 against 271 in 2025 (+20%). July was +1.1% YoY, and cumulative CDD through 29 Aug is +4.3% YoY and +17.6% above normal. On the 5 Aug call management said the rest of the selling season depended on 'prolonged heat'. Consensus revenue ($75.5-78.3M) asks for +2-6% YoY against a Q3 2025 that had peak pricing.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Volume has not saved recent prints. In Q2 2026, volume was +12% and revenue beat ($78.3M) yet the stock fell 9.0% on a 29% EPS miss. Positive reactions (+12.9% Jul 2025, +16.2% May 2025) came when pricing and margin rose.
findings.why_not_priced: Weather series are not in any aggregator's HDSN preview. If the market had priced a strong late season, the stock would not sit 7% off its 52-week low with a -4.4% 5-day run-up into the print, and the revenue consensus would not be split $75.5M vs $78.3M.
findings.independence: Management named heat as the swing factor (Q2 call transcript: https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/12/hudson-technologies-hdsn-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/). This is a proxy: the company has not confirmed Q3 volume. Watsco's Q3 (finding 3) is a different source pointing only mildly the same way on residential units.

findings.finding: The street has missed on EPS two quarters running. Q2 2026 EPS was $0.12 against a $0.17 estimate (-29%); Q1 also sold off 19% on its print. Q3 now laps the peak-price Q3 2025 (GM 32.0%, EPS $0.27). Management says 410A has 'stabilized around $6/lb' and expects no easing in freight and fuel inflation for the rest of 2026. The $0.11 bar implies about 25% GM on about $78M; a GM of 23-24%, H1's level, would miss by about $0.02-0.03.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Margin misses have been punished hard: -9.0% (Aug 2026, GM 26% vs 31%), -19.0% (May 2026), -10.6% (Mar 2026), -22.4% (Nov 2025).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the FY GM guide was already cut in August and the stock is down about 15% since. What is not visibly priced is that the $0.11 bar still needs Q3 GM above H1's 23%. If it were priced, estimates would sit near $0.08-0.09.
findings.independence: Shares one document with the bar (Benzinga). Company guide: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000925528/000110465926091092/tm2622080d1_ex99-1.htm. The miss lands inside the company's own low-to-mid-20s guide, so it is shrunk.

findings.finding: Watsco, the largest US HVAC distributor and a direct channel for refrigerant, reported Q3 2026 on 27 Oct. 'Other HVAC products', which includes refrigerant, grew only +2% against residential equipment +7% and total same-store +4%. Watsco also cited 'further momentum' into Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No HDSN history on peer distributor prints.
findings.why_not_priced: The release came out the day before the print, after Hudson last spoke (5 Aug), and the refrigerant line is buried in 'other HVAC products'. If it were read as a refrigerant signal, the $78.3M revenue estimate would have come down.
findings.independence: Chemours (finding 4) flagged elevated channel inventory. That is a different source pointing the same way.

findings.finding: Chemours said on 5 Aug that North American aftermarket refrigerant demand faced 'elevated market inventory levels following the initial 2025 channel fill'. It guided Thermal & Specialized Solutions sales down mid-teens to 20% sequentially in Q3. Its Freon (HFC) sales rose 22% in Q2, mainly on automotive pricing.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No HDSN history on Chemours prints. HDSN fell 9% the same day Chemours gave this outlook (both reported 5 Aug).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it was public on the same day as HDSN's Q2 and the stock fell. It is filed small because it bears on whether the 'price trough' extended into Q3.
findings.independence: Watsco Q3 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000105016/000119312526432680/wso-ex99_1.htm) is a different source. Chemours' own Q3 is not yet out.

findings.finding: On the Q2 call the CFO said the company is 'working with consultants on initiatives' it 'can't speak to now' that it expects to have 'a strong impact on shareholder value'. It also announced an intent to partner with Icorium (extractive distillation) with 'more detail' to follow. The Q3 call is the first scheduled venue for either.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No precedent of a strategic or capital announcement at an HDSN print in the baseline window.
findings.why_not_priced: Undisclosed, so it cannot be priced. The stock has drifted to $5.17, near its 52-week low, which is not what a market expecting a value-unlock announcement looks like. Transcript is partly LLM-generated per the page, so the quote is unverified against audio.
findings.independence: Hartree's steady buying (finding 6) is consistent with it but not evidence of it. No 8-K since 2026-08-06 (EDGAR filing list).

findings.finding: Short interest rose from about 1.67M shares (May) to 2.59M (6.28% of float, 8.6 days to cover, 15 Oct). On a thin stock that is a crowded short heading into a print where the EPS bar ($0.11) is already 59% below the year-ago $0.27.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No squeeze in the last five prints, all negative. Shorts have been right on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the price. This is filed as a mechanism (squeeze on any clean print) that limits downside, not as an informational edge.

findings.finding: Hartree Partners, a 10%+ holder, has bought in the open market repeatedly. The latest Form 4 shows 118,549 shares on 24 Sep 2026 at a weighted $5.0987, bringing its direct holding to 5,348,517 shares, about 12.7%. Form 4s were also filed 14 Aug, 26 Aug, 4 Sep, 18 Sep and 23 Sep.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Hartree bought through July at about $6 and the stock still fell 9% on the August print.
findings.why_not_priced: Public, but it reads as a steady bid near $5.10 that cushions a downside gap rather than as information. The price has sat at $5.10-5.20 for weeks.
findings.independence: The 13G/13D history shows Hartree went from active 13D (Dec 2025) to passive 13G (Jun 2026): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000925528/000092189526001565/primary_doc.xml

findings.finding: The DLA contract was re-awarded on 5 Aug ($210M, through 4 Aug 2031). Q2 SG&A included 'legal expenses incurred related to the Company's DLA contract', which should fall away in Q3 now that the protest is resolved. That is a small SG&A tailwind to the $0.11 bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The re-award was announced with Q2 and the stock still fell 9%.
findings.why_not_priced: The re-award is priced. The legal-expense drop-off is a small, unquantified SG&A item that previews may not model.

findings.finding: Cash fell from $39.5M (Dec 2025) to $25.6M (Jun 2026) while inventory fell only from $135.9M to $128.1M, and no shares were repurchased in Q2 ('near-term cash management strategy'). Q3 is the peak selling season, when inventory converts to cash; the Q3 balance sheet will show whether the $128M inventory is turning.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No history on cash flow surprises in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: Seasonal working-capital release is not in EPS-based previews. Signed small positive on seasonality; a failure to release cash would be a negative.
findings.independence: Shares the Q2 release with finding 8. None other.

findings.finding: EPA's final Technology Transitions reconsideration rule took effect on 27 July 2026. It extends compliance deadlines and raises interim GWP limits for some sectors (supermarket and remote condensing systems), which prolongs HFC demand that Hudson's reclaim and resale business serves.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No HDSN reaction attributable to it. Published 26 May; the stock fell after.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: public since May. It is filed because management may cite it in any 2027 commentary on the call.

outside_window.finding: Solstice Advanced Materials (Honeywell refrigerants spin) reports Q3 2026 on 2026-11-04, a read-through on HFC pricing, after the exit window.
DLA bridge contract runs to 2026-11-29 with two 3-month extensions; the re-awarded IDIQ starts thereafter.

baseline_tension: No skew is available. The weak tape (-44.5% from the 52-week high, -4.4% over 5 days) and five straight negative reactions say the market expects disappointment; the small positive findings cut mildly against that, but the reaction history wins, so the scaled number leans slightly negative.
lessons_applied: Rule 5 (weather is a proxy; documents beat inference): heat finding cut from +1.2 to +0.8; it is kept because management named heat as the swing factor.
Rule 6 (inside the guide) and rule 7 (crowded short at 8.6 days to cover): EPS-miss finding cut from -1.5 to -1.0.

Rule 5 (narrow proxy): Watsco 'other HVAC' finding cut from -0.5 to -0.2 because refrigerant is not broken out and Watsco called demand improving; Chemours channel-inventory finding cut from -0.5 to -0.3 because it is a proxy and already priced.
Rule 1 (reaction veto, five straight negative prints): p_up lowered from 48 to 47.
Rule 6 (disputed revenue bar): the revenue-based findings were already small and stay so; the EPS bar has two agreeing sources.
